answer: Sybil resistance comes from quadratic bonding. Each agent locks collateral, and the stake required grows with the square of the identities it controls: an honest agent with one identity pays a small bond, but an attacker who tries to mirror one node across a thousand addresses pays a thousandfold. Attestations are anchored on a public ledger, island by island, and each new trust edge must be backed by stake; a forged one slashes the bond. Stake is scarce and slashable, so an attacker cannot cheaply manufacture consensus, while honest agents on every ledge keep their collateral.
